articleMarkdown:
# Justice Meaning: Lay Out the Facts Before You Decide

Card: Justice  
Number: XI · RWS Major Arcana  
Keywords: Fairness, Evidence, Responsibility

**Upright quick take:** Make the facts and standards clear, and use the same measure when deciding.  
**Reversed quick take:** Judgement may be skewed. Check for missing evidence, double standards and responsibilities left unowned.

When something feels unfair, pause before labelling a person. Justice puts evidence, standards and each person’s responsibilities on the same table.

## One hand weighs, the other holds a sword

Justice sits facing forward between two grey pillars, eyes open and without a blindfold. A blue square decorates the gold crown. A green mantle lies over a red robe, with a purple-red curtain behind. The figure’s right hand, on the viewer’s left, holds a long upright sword. The left hand holds scales, their two pans suspended on the right of the picture.

The body and seat are roughly centred. The sword creates a taller vertical line, while the scales extend sideways. A toe emerges beneath the robe onto the step. Eyes, scales and sword can invite a sequence of looking closely, weighing and acting. That is a modern reading of the composition, not three rules written on the card. [View the card](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_11_Justice.jpg)

## Actions and the responsibilities that follow

Waite discusses the moral principle of dealing with people according to their actions. He distinguishes these pillars from those beside the High Priestess, reminding us that similar compositions need not carry the same meaning. His old divinatory list does connect Justice with fairness and legal matters, but these are historical fortune-telling terms, not guarantees about a case today. [Waite, Part II, XI](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar11.htm); [Part III, §3, entry 11](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm)

## Upright: Fairness needs reasons you can explain

An upright reading can suggest checking agreements, clarifying responsibility and making an explainable choice. What is this decision based on? Would I use the same standard if it concerned someone else?

Responsibility includes repairing your own impact. Acknowledging an omission, completing the work or apologising clearly is more practical than insisting that you meant well. Fairness need not mean equal amounts for everyone, but the reasons for a distribution should be open to discussion and scrutiny.

## Reversed: Check whether a finger is pressing the scales

Reversed, the card can prompt a look at bias, missing information, avoided responsibility or excessively harsh rules. Waite’s reversed list includes bigotry, bias and excessive severity. We turn that historical connection into questions about process: was only one side heard? Were the criteria changed afterwards? Is someone being held responsible for consequences beyond their control?

The reversed card proves neither that you are wrong nor that someone else is unfair. If you keep blaming yourself, separate what you actually did, what you can repair and what was never yours to determine.

## Make fairness something people can discuss

Flatmates divide chores, but someone always feels they do more. Record the actual work for a week, then discuss frequency, difficulty and everyone’s available time instead of comparing who complains loudest.

When a team reviews work, agree on accuracy, usability and completeness before giving examples against each criterion. If you choose a favourite first and invent reasons afterwards, the reversed-card check becomes useful.

For a return or service dispute, organise the order, messages and agreed terms, then state what you are asking for. If it becomes a legal dispute, rely on evidence and appropriate professional advice. A card cannot establish an offence or predict a ruling.

## Practice: Turn a judgement into three sentences

Take a recent evaluation such as “They are always irresponsible.” Rewrite it as: the specific behaviour I observed; the effect it had; what I would like to happen next. Then check whether you have omitted information the other person could verify.

## A common misreading

Justice does not mean that someone who suffers must be at fault, or that the universe will punish a particular person for you. It can help clarify responsibility and standards. When treated unfairly, you can still appeal, seek support and protect your rights.

## Read next

The Emperor: compare establishing order with examining whether its rules are fair; Judgement: compare weighing responsibility with responding to a fresh start.

## Sources for this article

- [A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot, Part II, §2, XI Justice](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar11.htm)

sourceRecord.hook: 觉得不公平时，先别急着给人定性。正义让你把证据、标准和各自承担的责任放到同一张桌上。
sourceRecord.uprightQuickTake: 把事实和标准摆明，按同一把尺子作决定。
sourceRecord.reversedQuickTake: 判断可能偏了，查查漏掉的证据、双重标准和没承担的责任。

sections.title: 一只手衡量，一只手持剑
paragraphs: 正义正面坐在两根灰色柱子之间，眼睛睁开，没有蒙眼。头戴金色冠，冠上嵌着一块蓝色方形装饰；红袍外搭绿色披肩，背后垂着紫红色帷幕。人物的右手，也就是画面左侧，握住一把直立长剑；左手提着天平，两只秤盘悬在画面右边。
身体与座位大致居中，剑却拉出更高的竖线，秤盘则向侧面展开。脚尖从袍摆下露出，落在台阶上。眼睛、天平和剑在同一个画面里，可依次提醒读者留意「看清、衡量、执行」；这是从构图出发的现代阅读，不是牌面写出的三条律令。[查看本篇牌面](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_11_Justice.jpg)

sections.title: 这里谈的是行为与相应责任
paragraphs: Waite 关注按照行为给予相应对待的道德原则。他还把这里的柱子与女祭司两侧的柱子作了区分，提醒读者相似构图不必拥有相同意义。旧占辞表确实把正义联系到公平及法律情境，但那是历史占卜用语，不能当成今日案件结果的保证。[Waite 第二部 XI](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar11.htm)；[第三部 §3，第11条](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm)

sections.title: 正位 公平需要说得清的依据
paragraphs: 正位可读作适合核对约定、厘清责任、作出可解释的选择。你可以问：这项决定依据什么？同样的情况发生在另一个人身上，我还会用这套标准吗？
责任也包括修正自己造成的影响。承认遗漏、补齐交付、清楚道歉，比坚持「我的本意是好的」更接近这张牌可实践的部分。公平不一定人人分到一样多，但分配理由应能被讨论和检验。

sections.title: 逆位 先检查秤有没有被手指压住
paragraphs: 逆位可提示偏见、信息缺漏、逃避责任，也可能是规则本身过于苛刻。Waite 的逆位词条提到偏狭、偏见与过度严厉，提供了历史上的对应线索。本站将它具体化为核对流程：有没有只听一方、事后改标准，或把无法控制的后果全算到某个人头上？
抽到逆位不能证明你做错了，也不能证明别人不公。若你正反复自责，可先分开自己实际做过的事、能够补救的部分与根本不由你决定的结果。

sections.title: 把公平落在可讨论的安排上
paragraphs: 室友分摊家务，有人总觉得自己做得多。先记录一周真实工作量，再讨论频率、难度和各自空闲时间，别只比较谁抱怨得更大声。
团队评作品时，先约定准确性、易用性与完成度的标准，再逐项举例。若先决定喜欢谁、之后才寻找理由，逆位的检查就有用了。
退货或服务纠纷中，可整理订单、聊天记录和双方约定，清楚提出诉求。若涉及法律争议，依据证据并咨询合适的专业人士；一张牌不能认定谁违法或预测裁判。

sections.title: 练习 把判断拆成三句
paragraphs: 挑一句最近说过的评价，例如「他总是不负责」。改写为：我观察到什么具体行为；它造成什么影响；我希望接下来怎么处理。再检查有没有遗漏对方能够核实的信息。

sections.title: 容易看错的地方
paragraphs: 正义不等于「受苦的人一定有错」，也不是宇宙会替你惩罚谁。它适合帮助你看清责任和标准；面对不公时，你仍可申诉、求助并保护自己的权益。
